Plot an evaluation

Source: R/verb-evaluate.R
plot.survalis_eval.Rd

type = "metrics" draws one panel per metric with the per-split values as a box plot and points; each panel has its own value axis and its strip says whether higher or lower is better. type = "time" draws the time-specific metrics ("brier" evaluated at several times, stored as "brier@<time>") against time: the mean over the splits with its 95% interval, or the single value when the predictions were scored once.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'survalis_eval'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("metrics", "time"),
  reference = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  xlab = "Time",
  time.labels = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A survalis_eval object.

type

"metrics" (default) or "time".

reference

For type = "time": an optional second survalis_eval on the same times, drawn dashed in grey, for example the Kaplan-Meier curve given to everyone (evaluate() on a matrix).

labels

For type = "time": legend labels of x and reference. NULL uses their model names.

xlab

For type = "time": the time axis label.

time.labels

For type = "time": NULL labels the evaluation times as they are; a function maps them to labels, e.g. function(t) t / 365.

title, subtitle, caption

Plot title, subtitle and caption; NULL (default) draws none.

...

Unused.

Value

A ggplot.

Examples

m <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, veteran, "coxph")
ev <- evaluate(m, times = c(30, 90, 180), resampling = cv(3, seed = 1),
               metrics = c("cindex", "brier"))
plot(ev)

km <- summary(survival::survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, veteran), times = c(30, 90, 180))$surv
ref <- evaluate(matrix(km, nrow(veteran), 3, byrow = TRUE),
                y = Surv(veteran$time, veteran$status), times = c(30, 90, 180),
                metrics = "brier")
plot(ev, type = "time", reference = ref, labels = c("Cox model", "Kaplan-Meier"),
     xlab = "Days")
